name: Oleafly v0.4.9
body:
## What's new in 0.4.9

### Added

- The interface speaks Vietnamese. Choose Tiếng Việt under
  Settings > General > Language, or leave the language on System default and
  Oleafly follows your computer. The collaboration server, the browser
  project page, the sign-in pages it serves and the file manager's
  Open with Oleafly action are translated as well.
- Cloud sync works with Google Drive and S3-compatible storage as well as
  Dropbox (#317). Choose one under Settings > Data storage > Cloud sync.
  Google Drive keeps your projects in an Oleafly folder in My Drive. Files you
  delete go to Google Drive's trash, and Oleafly checks Drive for changes from
  your other computers once a minute. For S3 you enter the endpoint, the
  bucket and your keys. Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage with HMAC keys and
  MinIO all work. Before it connects, Oleafly tries a few writes in the
  bucket. A service that ignores conditional writes is turned down, because
  without them two computers syncing at once could overwrite each other. When
  two computers change the same file at the same moment, the one that syncs
  second keeps both versions.
- Storage usage has a bar of everything in the Oleafly data folder, split by
  what takes the space. Below it, each part has its size: documents and code,
  images, PDFs, Git history, build cache, the TeX distribution, tools Oleafly
  downloaded such as Typst and Quarto, AI agents, research tasks, checkpoints
  and the rest.
- Cut, Copy, Paste and Select all in the editor's right-click menu (#319).
  Formatting, inserting, and import and export each moved into a submenu, so
  the menu is much shorter. In Markdown files, type `/table` or `/equation`
  to insert one, as LaTeX and Typst files already allowed. The Ask AI popup
  also takes your own request next to the preset actions.
- Oleafly's MCP server is in the MCP Registry as `io.github.Oleafly/oleafly`.
  Each release carries `oleafly.mcpb`, which installs it in Claude Desktop
  when you open it. It runs the `oleafly` command the app installs, so you
  need the app with Settings > Integrations > Oleafly MCP turned on.
- A CLI agent that is still starting has a Cancel button.
- Suggesting mode for shared projects. Switch the editor from Editing to
  Suggesting and your edits become tracked changes: added text is
  highlighted, and deleted text stays visible, struck through. Owners and
  editors accept or reject each suggestion, or every suggestion in a file at
  once, and whoever suggested a change can withdraw it. The Comments pane
  lists suggestions next to the comments, and you can reply to one like a
  comment.
  AI edits and inserted citations made while suggesting become suggestions
  too. A compile or export with suggestions waiting tells you how many. One
  suggested deletion can be up to 20,000 characters. Delete more than that at
  once and the text comes back, with a note that says why.
- Reviewer and Commenter roles for shared projects. A reviewer comments and
  suggests changes, and every edit they make is a suggestion. A commenter
  reads and comments. Both can use the chat. You can give these roles to
  people you add, to guests and to the project's link. The server checks
  every change a reviewer or commenter sends, so an edit their role doesn't
  allow never reaches anyone.
- A chat for each shared project, in a Chat tab next to Comments. Everyone
  but viewers can post, people can delete their own messages, and the owner can
  clear the chat.
- History for shared projects, in the collaboration pane. It lists changes by
  time and person. Open any version to read it, compare two versions, restore
  one file or the whole project, or give a version a name such as "Sent to
  the reviewers". Owners and editors restore and name versions. Restoring the
  whole project brings back every file's text and the files deleted since.
  Renamed files keep their new names, figures and files added later stay as
  they are, and suggestions made after that version are dropped. A restore is
  a new change, so the text it replaces stays in the history.
- Add server now offers the Oleafly server as a one-click choice above the
  address field. Any other server's address still works as before.
- Co-authors can open a shared project in their browser when the
  collaboration server has browser access turned on. Without installing
  Oleafly, they can edit as their role allows, comment, handle suggestions,
  chat and read the latest PDF, and the project's web page gets an **Open in
  browser** button. Whoever runs the server turns it on with
  `OLEAFLY_WEB=true`, and the published server image already includes the
  browser app.
- After a successful compile of a shared project's main document, an owner's
  or editor's app uploads the PDF and its SyncTeX file to the server, at most
  once a minute, so people reading the project in a browser see the newest
  PDF and who compiled it. The uploaded SyncTeX file names files only by
  their place in the project. A build that read files you keep out of the
  shared project isn't uploaded.
- In the browser, click a word in the compiled PDF to open the source line
  it came from, or press Show in PDF (Ctrl+Shift+J, or Cmd+Shift+J on a Mac)
  to find the line you're on in the PDF. It works with the PDF and SyncTeX
  file the app uploads, whichever computer compiled them.
- Oleafly Server's `OLEAFLY_WEB_CONNECT_SRC` lists the other sites the
  browser app may connect to, by default `https://mirrors.oleafly.com`.
- Oleafly Server can let anyone sign up. With `OLEAFLY_OPEN_SIGNUP=true`,
  anyone who signs in with one of the server's sign-in options gets an
  account, and each account gets 100 MB of storage, 50 shared projects and
  300 uploads an hour. `OLEAFLY_ACCOUNT_STORAGE_MB`,
  `OLEAFLY_MAX_PROJECTS_PER_ACCOUNT` and `OLEAFLY_UPLOADS_PER_HOUR` change
  those limits, and also work without open sign-up. Compiled PDFs count
  toward storage but not toward uploads.
- Quarto and Calepin engines. Quarto turns `.qmd` and `.Rmd` documents into a
  PDF, a web page or slides, and Calepin runs the code in a Typst document
  and puts the results in the PDF. Oleafly uses the copy on your computer, or
  downloads a pinned, checksum-verified one from Settings > Engines when you
  ask. Code runs with your own R, Python or Julia, and only after you allow
  code for that project in the Compile menu. Until then Quarto shows the code
  without running it, and Calepin shows the results from its last run. New
  templates: Quarto article, Quarto slides and Calepin report. Quarto's
  working folders (`.quarto` and a document's `_files` folder) stay out of
  cloud sync, shared projects and checkpoints. Calepin's `.calepin` folder is
  shared and synced like any other, so co-authors who haven't allowed code
  still see its stored results.
- When a Typst document has Chinese, Japanese or Korean text that no font on
  this computer can show, Oleafly says so and offers to download the free
  font pack that covers it.
- **Add custom provider** in Settings > AI has presets for Qwen (DashScope),
  Kimi (Moonshot), Zhipu GLM, SiliconFlow and Volcengine Ark. Pick one and it
  fills in the name and base URL, so you only add your API key.
- **App icon**, a section below Theme customization in Settings > Appearance,
  offers eleven icons for the Dock or taskbar while Oleafly is open: classic,
  pastel, blue, light, prism, iridescent, ocean, mint, aurora, sunset and
  coral. Classic, the green quill, is still the default. The quill next to the
  Oleafly name and the one on the startup screen take on the colours of the
  icon you pick.
- Template authors can give their own Typst functions a form. Describe the
  arguments in `[tool.oleafly]` in a package's `typst.toml`, or in
  `oleafly-forms.toml` at the project root, and Visual mode shows each call as
  a card with labelled fields. Inside a paragraph, the call is a chip that
  opens the same fields. Changing a field rewrites only that argument. A field
  can hold text, Typst markup, a choice from a list, a number or an on/off
  switch. Mistakes in `oleafly-forms.toml`, or in the `typst.toml` of a
  package vendored into the project, show as markers when you open the file.

### Changed

- Document settings reads Typst strings the way Typst does: an unknown escape
  such as `\q`, or a `\u{..}` that names no character, stays as written.
- CLI agents are no longer marked beta.
- Errors from CLI agents, such as a disconnect, a timeout, a missing Node.js
  or a refused file request, now show in your interface language instead of
  English, with the agent's own last output kept as it was.
- DeepSeek thinks during assistant runs again. Oleafly now keeps each reply's
  reasoning and sends it back, which DeepSeek requires once tools are in use,
  and the effort menu offers Off, Low, High and Max for DeepSeek models.
  Chats saved before this change keep thinking off for tool runs.
- Cost estimates, budgets and research task spending limits count DeepSeek's
  peak rates, which are double the off-peak rates on weekdays from 01:00 to
  04:00 and 06:00 to 10:00 UTC.
- Agents started from the Dock, Finder or Start menu get the proxy settings,
  API keys and endpoints you set in your shell profile, such as
  `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` or `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. A value Oleafly
  already has wins, keys are hidden in transcripts and errors, and traffic to
  Oleafly's own tool servers skips the proxy. Research tasks get the proxy
  settings but not the keys.
- Installing an agent bridge uses the registry, proxy and certificate
  settings from your `.npmrc`. An unreachable registry fails within about a
  minute and the message names it, and large bridges get 15 minutes to
  download.
- Claude Code's bridge is now 0.95.0.
- "Let agents use my Oleafly API keys" can send Claude Code through a
  DeepSeek or Z.ai key, using their Anthropic-compatible endpoints. Codex is
  only offered your OpenAI key, the only kind it accepts.
- Codex can use your own Codex CLI when it is at least as new as the one its
  bridge bundles, and starts in the mode you last picked.
- Oleafly loads less code when it starts. Settings, the tour guide, the
  diagram composer and most dialogs load the first time you open them. PDF
  page rendering loads when something first needs it, and KaTeX when you
  first open a LaTeX or Markdown file. Once you've finished the tours, the
  library screen loads about 2 MB less. Mermaid diagrams in chat use the
  app's KaTeX instead of bundling an older copy. Cloud sync only loads its
  background code on a computer connected to Dropbox, Google Drive or an S3
  bucket, or once you open Settings.
- GitLab, Codeberg, Gitea and Forgejo accounts show their real logos, GitLab's
  and Codeberg's in their own colours: in the add-account choices, in
  Settings, in the remote menu, in the publish dialog and beside each
  repository. The publish dialog's account picker moved to
  the bottom left, beside the button.
- In Settings, each Git hosting account keeps its actions on the right and
  signs out with an icon button. The server name shows only when it differs
  from the badge.
- Live collaboration is no longer an experiment and is always on. Settings >
  Collaboration is there from the start, and the switch under Settings >
  Experimentation is gone.
- With Oleafly in Chinese, DeepSeek is the suggested AI provider. It comes
  first in the provider list and is preselected until you set up a provider.
- Desktop apps is now called Computer Use. Its tab in Settings > Integrations
  has a cursor icon and comes after Oleafly MCP, and the app picker shows
  each app's icon.
- Computer Use doesn't ask before each action anymore. Agents still reach
  only the apps and websites you list, and when you turn Computer Use on,
  Oleafly first tells you that actions will run without asking. To approve
  each click, keystroke, page change and script, turn on Ask before each
  action in Settings > Integrations > Computer Use. If Computer Use was
  already on when you updated, Ask before each action stays on until you turn
  it off.
- Choosing Full access in the chat's approval menu applies right away,
  without a confirmation dialog.

### Fixed

- Scrolling the new project gallery after downloading a template from a pack
  no longer crashes the app (#359). If a dialog or panel does run into an
  error, only that part closes now and the details go to the log. Before, the
  whole window switched to the crash screen.
- PubMed ID lookups and PubMed literature search keep working when PubMed's
  summary service is down. Oleafly then gets the records from NCBI's
  citation exporter. Before, Add citation and `oleaflyc cite` said PubMed had
  no record for a real paper, and search showed no PubMed results.
- Computer Use works with Cua Driver 0.38, the version its installer gives
  you now. Oleafly refused to start every 0.38 driver, saying it wasn't
  running with Oleafly's limits, because 0.38 words that check's answer
  differently.
- Computer Use can find the windows of the apps you allowed again. Cua
  Driver 0.38 refuses to list every app or window, so agents saw nothing and
  were told the app wasn't allowed. Oleafly now finds the allowed apps that
  run and asks for their windows one app at a time.
- Computer Use only opens apps on your list. Cua Driver 0.38 opens any app
  it's asked to, so Oleafly now checks the app first.
- Clicks and typing in an allowed app work again. Cua Driver 0.38 refuses
  them unless the call names the app's process, and agents usually name only
  the window or element they saw, so you could approve an action and then
  watch it fail. Oleafly now adds the process the driver reported for that
  window.
- Websites in Computer Use work with Cua Driver 0.38. The driver now acts
  in a tab only after it binds the browser's window, and agents had no way
  to do that, so every page change was refused. Oleafly now connects to the
  browser it opened, fills in the tab on later calls and passes the page's
  text to the agent. A site that isn't on your list is turned down before
  you're asked.
- An agent on a model that reads only text, such as GLM-5.3, no longer
  fails when a tool returns a picture, for example a Computer Use
  screenshot. The provider turned the whole request down. Now the picture is
  left out and the model works from the text.
- More code editors can't be added to Computer Use, because they run code
  or commands without asking you: Sublime Text, BBEdit, Nova, Xcode,
  Antigravity, Kiro, MacVim and Emacs.
- Computer Use's setup is clearer. Settings asks for the macOS permissions
  only once Cua Driver is installed and new enough, says when Cua Driver
  hasn't checked them yet instead of "couldn't read", and shows the grant
  command to copy when no project is open. After you run a step in the
  terminal, Settings opens on Computer Use again, and the command in the
  terminal's confirmation wraps instead of running off the edge. A Cua Driver
  start that stops at its own permissions prompt says so.
- The Oleafly icon no longer looks bigger than other apps' icons in the Dock
  and Finder on macOS 15 and earlier. The bundled icon now leaves the margin
  macOS expects around an app icon.
- Deleting a file or folder in the file tree asks first again, and so do
  restoring an earlier chat checkpoint and replacing an equation or diagram
  file. The question never showed up in the app, so all of these went ahead
  without asking. That included the permanent delete on a system with no
  trash.
- CLI agents and research tasks keep your NO_PROXY list when you set only one
  spelling of it. On Linux and macOS the other spelling held only the local
  addresses, and agents that read it sent internal hosts through your proxy.
- In Typst document settings, clearing two values of one `#set` rule, or
  clearing one and setting another, could leave a broken rule such as
  `#set par(` without its closing parenthesis. Clearing a value on the line
  after a `//` comment, or in a rule written with its commas first, could
  break the rule too.
- In a Typst table cell, one bracket without its pair turned every bracket in
  the cell into plain text, and a cell that ended in `\` broke the table. A
  `$` without its pair, as in a price like `$5`, a `//` or `/*`, or a lone
  backtick broke the table too, and did the same to a figure caption. Now
  only what has no pair is escaped. No borders also works when the table's
  `stroke` value comes after a comment.
- In a Visual mode table cell, Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on macOS) undid the document
  instead of your typing in the cell, and Ctrl+B or Ctrl+I added bold or
  italic markup somewhere else in the text.
- Vendor packages skipped a package whose name has capital letters or other
  letters Typst allows, such as `@local/AcmeReport:1.0.0`.
- Custom providers that need no API key, such as a local Lemonade, LM Studio
  or llama.cpp server, stopped working after the first save. Oleafly lost the
  "no key needed" setting when it saved, so every request failed with "No API
  key is set". It now keeps the setting and repairs providers saved by
  earlier versions.
- With a key-less custom provider selected, the assistant showed "Connect a
  provider", and picking one of its models in the chat hid the message box.
- Adding a custom provider now fetches its model list first and tells you
  what went wrong if that fails, for example that the server isn't running or
  the key was refused. An address entered without /v1, like
  `http://localhost:13305`, is saved as `http://localhost:13305/v1` when that
  is where the models are. You can still add a provider that lists no models
  and type the model names yourself.
- The custom provider dialog turns down a base URL that has your key or a `?`
  in it, and tells you to put the key in the API key field (#344).
- When a custom provider had no models, requests went to another provider you
  had set up, which could be a cloud one, without any sign. Now the assistant
  says the provider needs a model.
- A model that took a while to load on its first request, or a server that
  was briefly unreachable, got marked as unable to use tools until you
  checked it again. Now only the model's actual answer decides that. Local
  and custom servers get two minutes to answer the check, and models that
  were blocked this way get checked again.
- A model that failed the tool check is still used for requests that need no
  tools. Before, Oleafly refused those too (#344).
- When you changed a custom provider's address, the dialog said the saved key
  would be sent to the new one, but Oleafly removed it. The dialog now says
  the key stays behind: enter it again, or leave it blank for a server that
  needs no key.
- Custom providers now appear in the inline edit model picker. Research tasks
  and the Tools converters work with custom providers that need no key, and
  Image to LaTeX works offline with one running on your computer.
- If a local server sends an error partway through a reply, Oleafly shows
  that error instead of "The connection closed".
- The single API key from early versions is no longer sent to a custom
  provider.
- A base URL pasted with /chat/completions or /models on the end is trimmed.
- Some local models, such as Bonsai-4B on Lemonade, write a tool call into
  the reply as plain text, like `{"name": "ping", "arguments": {}} </tool_call>`.
  Oleafly showed that text as the answer, and the tool check said the model
  couldn't use tools. It now runs a call written this way when the call names
  a tool Oleafly offered and has valid JSON arguments. Any other reply stays
  text. A reply that starts like a tool call appears once it is finished
  instead of word by word.
- DeepSeek Harness couldn't open a conversation and said "The agent
  disconnected." It prints a log line on its output while a session starts,
  and Oleafly closed the connection at the first line that wasn't a protocol
  message. Oleafly now skips such lines and shows them with the agent's other
  output if something goes wrong.
- DeepSeek Harness is found in its usual install folder on macOS and Windows
  when `dsh` isn't on your PATH, and a missing or rejected DeepSeek key now
  shows its sign-in steps.
- Pressing Enter or New conversation while an agent was starting launched a
  second copy and left the first one running. Messages sent during a start
  now wait for it.
- Hermes with no model provider set up said only "Internal error". Oleafly
  shows Hermes's own message and its setup steps. Picking a model no longer
  removes Oleafly's research tools from Hermes, a conversation from another
  Hermes profile says so when you reopen it, and Settings shows the installed
  Hermes version even when GitHub is slow or unreachable.
- Pi gave a blank reply when its model provider failed. Oleafly now shows
  the provider's error, and any agent that ends a turn without replying says
  so. Pi no longer shows two pickers with the same choices, and an older
  `pi-acp` on your PATH isn't used.
- Claude Code disconnected when it asked to write a file larger than about
  half a megabyte. The permission card now opens without the preview.
- Reopening a conversation that never got a message failed with Claude Code
  and DeepSeek Harness. It now starts again.
- After reconnecting, Codex went back to its default mode and model, and
  Claude Code to its default effort. Oleafly now restores the model, mode
  and effort the conversation had, and remembers the model you pick.
- Codex asked you to sign in when the real problem was its `config.toml` or
  a rejected key from another provider. Oleafly now shows Codex's own error
  or names the provider and its key variable. Failed Codex turns no longer
  look like normal replies.
- Claude Code users with their own API endpoint were told to sign in to
  Anthropic, and the account line read "Signed in with Not logged in".
- A CLI agent that crashed while starting, for example on a network
  timeout, asked you to sign in when its error output happened to contain a
  word like "OAuth" or "unauthorized", as file paths in a stack trace often
  do. Oleafly now shows the crash, and asks you to sign in only when the
  agent itself says so.
- Permission requests expired after two minutes. They now wait for you, and
  a request for a file outside the project is refused with a note naming it.
- A failed start left an empty conversation in History.
- Hermes couldn't reach Oleafly's research tools behind an HTTP proxy, and a
  stalled tool server could hold up a start for minutes.
- Agent errors on Windows set to a language without UTF-8 output came out
  garbled, Node.js warnings could hide the real error, and a timed-out start
  dropped the agent's last output.
- Some agent errors, such as asking you to trust the folder, showed as raw
  codes.
- On DeepSeek, a reply cut short when DeepSeek ran out of capacity now
  retries or shows an error, and long tool calls are no longer cut off at
  about 8,000 tokens. DeepSeek Flash is treated as reading images.
- When the assistant's request times out, the provider has a server error,
  the request is turned down or the reply comes back empty, the error now
  tells you what to try next. This works with every provider (#338).
- When Tectonic crashed while looking for a font that isn't installed, the
  build failed with nothing in the error list, and only the last line of the
  log said the compiler had crashed. Tectonic 0.17 does this on some
  documents instead of reporting the missing font. The error list now names
  the font and the line Tectonic had reached, and suggests installing the
  font or switching to XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX. Other compiler crashes show an error
  too, in the app and from the `oleafly` command.
- The assistant saw only the start of a long command's output, without the
  exit code, and missed the error at the end. It now gets the exit code and
  the start and end of the output, and an error printed after a long log is
  kept.
- Open files in a library project reload when a terminal, an agent or
  another app changes them, as files in an opened folder already did. If you
  have unsaved edits, a bar above the editor lets you compare both versions,
  keep yours, or reload. When a save stops because the file changed on disk,
  you get the same bar instead of a separate message (#339).
- Some PDFs showed pages with images or text missing, or with colours a
  little off, because Oleafly didn't ship the extra files the PDF viewer
  needs for them. It now includes the standard fonts for PDFs that don't
  embed their own, decoders for the JPEG 2000 and JBIG2 images common in
  scans, the character maps some Chinese, Japanese and Korean fonts rely on,
  and the CMYK colour profile. The preview, presentation mode, PDF to
  LaTeX and PDFs you attach in the assistant all use them.
- On macOS and Windows, when `\input` spelled a file's name with other
  capitals than the file has, such as `\input{Chapters/Intro}` for
  `chapters/intro.tex`, Show in PDF and clicks in the PDF did nothing for
  that file, and its compile errors weren't marked in the editor. Oleafly now
  falls back to a match that ignores case when only one file fits.
- A Typst equation preview that failed for a reason outside the equation,
  such as a render that timed out during a long compile, kept showing that
  error until you changed the equation. It now tries again the next time the
  equation is drawn.
- App font size in Settings > Appearance now also sizes the editor's search
  bar buttons, the cards that open when you point at a label or command, and
  the Visual mode table's toolbar and dialogs. Their text used to stay the
  same size.
- In the Linux AppImage, the programs a build starts, such as a TeX Live
  installed on your system or Pandoc, still inherited the AppImage's
  library paths, which Git and the terminal stopped doing in 0.4.8. They now
  start without them.
- If getting Pandoc ready for a Markdown build failed after you had already
  switched to another project, that project's preview showed the Pandoc
  error instead of its own build.
- Disconnecting cloud sync during a long sync and then connecting another
  account within a few minutes could let the old sync keep going. It could
  bring back files you had deleted and add conflict copies, which the new
  account then uploaded, and an error from it could mark the new account as
  disconnected. Connecting now stops a running sync first, and a sync stops
  when the account changes.
- Clicking Apply again in a research task's details while its changes were
  being applied started a second apply. It now applies once.

### Security

- Updated zip, the library that reads and writes ZIP files, from 4.6.1 to
  9.1.3. Oleafly unpacks ZIP files you import and ones it downloads, such as
  TinyTeX, language servers, agent bridges and projects from an online LaTeX
  service. The update fixes several GitHub security advisories in zip. One is
  critical: zip could read an archive differently from other ZIP tools.
  Another, rated high, is about where a symbolic link in an archive points.
  The updater, tauri-plugin-updater, moved from 2.11.0 to 2.14.1 so it uses
  the new zip as well.
- Math in the assistant's replies now uses only KaTeX 0.18.7, the version the
  rest of the app uses. A Markdown math package still brought in KaTeX
  0.16.47, which has a security advisory (GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7).
- Updated zstd, the compression library behind file history and the file
  snapshots taken during agent turns, from 0.13.3 to 0.14.3. It fixes four
  security advisories in how zstd handles memory (RUSTSEC-2026-0391,
  RUSTSEC-2026-0398, RUSTSEC-2026-0403 and RUSTSEC-2026-0410).
- Updated pulldown-cmark, the Markdown parser behind spelling and grammar in
  `oleafly lint`, from 0.13.4 to 0.13.5 (#348). It fixes a security advisory
  where a small Markdown file with crafted wiki links could use up all
  memory (RUSTSEC-2026-0414).
- Saving an MCP server that runs a program on this computer asks first, in a
  system dialog that shows the command and names any environment variables
  it sets. It asks again when you change the program, its arguments or its
  environment. If you say no, the server isn't saved (#336).
- Each Oleafly window can only use the app commands it needs, and web pages
  shown inside Oleafly can use none. Exports, imports, checkpoint archives,
  skills, templates and other files outside a project only work with a file
  or folder you picked in a file dialog, or on Linux one you just dropped on
  the window. Saved connector keys, such as an alphaXiv key, no longer reach
  the app window (#336).
- With code off, Quarto reads all of a document's settings before it builds:
  every YAML block, `_quarto.yml`, `_metadata.yml` and any metadata files
  they name. If anything there could run a program, such as a Lua filter, a
  pre- or post-render script, an unusual PDF engine, an engine option like
  `-shell-escape` or a shortcode Quarto doesn't ship, Oleafly doesn't build
  and asks you to allow code. Inline R anywhere in the document or the files
  it includes counts as code too. Included files and metadata files must be
  inside the project.
- Oleafly Server checks comments and chat messages from reviewers and
  commenters whatever app they use, not only in the browser. They can add
  comments, replies and messages and change or delete their own, but they
  can't delete other people's or clear the chat.
- On a server that runs over https without a path prefix, the browser app's
  session cookie is now `__Host-oleafly_web`, so a site on another subdomain
  can't slip in a session of its own. If you already used the browser app on
  such a server, you sign in again once. Behind a path prefix, a browser that

body:
## What's new in 0.4.8

### Added

- The `oleafly` command. It builds, checks and inspects your projects from a
  terminal with the same compilers, settings and folders as the app, and
  every command can print one JSON result with stable error and exit codes
  for scripts and coding agents. Commands cover builds and watching, the
  project's map (`oleafly context`), word counts, exports and conversions,
  citations and bibliography cleanup, Typst versions, templates, the app's
  checkpoints and settings. Turn it on under Settings > General > Terminal
  command. On Windows, Install copies it into your user folder and adds it to
  your PATH. If an `oleafly` that Oleafly didn't make is already there,
  Replace it puts this copy in its place once you confirm. Oleafly's own
  terminal and the agents it starts have it on their PATH.
- `oleafly mcp`, an MCP server for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, Cursor
  and Gemini CLI. It needs no URL, token or Node.js. With the app open it
  passes calls to the app, with your approval rules; on its own it offers
  read tools and compiling. `oleafly mcp config --client NAME` prints or
  writes the setup. The bundled `oleafly-cli` skill teaches agents the
  commands.
- `oleafly check` runs Preflight from a terminal or CI, and `oleafly lint`
  runs the LaTeX, BibTeX, spelling and grammar checks. Both print people's
  text, JSON or SARIF for code scanning, and `--exit-code` fails a CI job on
  findings.
- `oleafly auth`, `oleafly remote` and `oleafly server`. Sign in to an
  online LaTeX service, download projects, and keep a folder in two-way sync
  through the service's Git bridge, with the same merge as the app and a
  marked-up latexdiff PDF of your changes. Sign the command line in to an
  Oleafly server as its own device to manage sharing and members and to read
  and write comments. Sign-ins live in the encrypted store the app uses.
- `oleafly ask` and `oleafly agent run` run the Oleafly agent on a project
  without opening the app. The agent can always read; `--allow` adds writing,
  commands or network access. Changes go to a review folder first, and
  `oleafly agent apply` writes them into the project.
- Research tasks are experimental in this release and off for everyone.
  Settings > Experimentation has the switch, with a warning next to it: runs
  can stall, fail or leave changes you have to sort out by hand, so turn them
  on at your own risk. Turning it on adds the Research tab and the Research
  section in Settings. While it is off, Files has no Task outputs, the
  assistant and outside agents get no task tools, and nothing moves to the
  background helper; turning it off again stops every running task. The
  assistant, the `oleafly` command and CLI agents do not depend on the
  switch.

  experiment runs included. Approvals wait for you with a notification, and
  the app takes the task back when you open it. Settings > Research >

  and shows, stops and logs it. Task details show In background or Moving
  back, and Show earlier activity loads what a task did before it moved.
  `oleafly daemon run`, `status` and `stop` work with the helper from a
  terminal.
- Research task briefs: a goal, success criteria, scope, a main metric and a
  budget for time, cost and runs. With Review the plan first, the agent
  writes `plan.md` and waits for your approval. Each task keeps a research
  record (plan, ledger, sources, hand-off and report) that comes back with its
  review and applies without a preview, long jobs run as runs
  with logs and metrics, and the Progress tab shows runs, the ledger and the
  budget. When a task finishes, Oleafly checks that the project builds, new
  references resolve, cited numbers match their runs and new figures are
  used. Tasks can start at a set time, and Resume continues where a task
  stopped.
- Remote compute for research tasks. Add SSH machines and Slurm clusters, or
  Cua Spaces, under Settings > Research > Compute, and send a task's runs
  there. Oleafly checks host keys, and Forget host key works for machines
  from your SSH config too. It reads your SSH config without changing it and
  never stores passwords or keys. Runs choose a profile: Analysis by
  default, or Training with GPUs and longer time limits.
- A Windows sandbox for research tasks, in beta and off by default. Commands
  run in an AppContainer that reaches only the task's files and the folders
  you allow. With it on, CLI agents can run as tasks on Windows too.
- Desktop apps. Agents can use the desktop programs and websites you allow,
  such as a journal's submission form or a statistics package, through Cua
  Driver, which you install yourself. Oleafly asks before each action unless
  you allow that kind of action for the chat, session or task, and your own
  signed-in browser and scripts always ask. Common browsers, terminals, code
  editors and password managers can't be added as apps. For a browser, add
  the websites instead. Set it up under Settings > Integrations > Desktop
  apps.

  Recent Claude and OpenAI models use their provider's search; other models
  search with a Brave, Tavily or Serper key you add in Settings.

  model's maximum, and a usage meter that shows the context used, tokens and
  cost of the conversation, with your provider's remaining credit where it
  reports one.

  dragging them into the composer (#305). PDFs send their text (up to 100
  pages) and page images where the model reads images.
- CLI agents: saved conversations with dates, search, rename and delete,
  exported as Markdown or JSON (#142); Hermes (#140), also on a remote
  machine; routing an agent's model calls through a key you pick; sign-in
  from Oleafly's terminal; the shared composer with attachments, effort and
  usage; text you select in the editor goes with your next message as a
  quote; and version 2 of the Agent Client Protocol, as an experiment.

  Codeberg and servers you run yourself, with an access token or, on
  github.com, a code in your browser. Publish to any connected account, link
  a project to any repository by its address, import from an account or clone
  by address, and use your organization's certificate authority. Push and
  pull explain SSH and credential problems in plain words.

  can use any model you've set up, a local Ollama model by default, or
  Mathpix with your own keys. A hosted choice says where your files go, and
  long scans show the page count and estimated cost before they start.

  select, what Shift+Enter sends and Option as Meta on macOS. Find in the
  terminal (Ctrl+Shift+F on Windows and Linux, so Ctrl+F still reaches the
  shell), a dot on a hidden tab when its program rings the bell, tab titles
  from programs, Open in terminal from the file tree, dragging files in to
  type their paths, and shortcuts for new, close, next and previous terminal.

  it, written the way that language writes links: `[name](<path>)` in
  Markdown, `#link("path")[name]` in Typst and `\href{path}{name}` in LaTeX,
  relative to the open document. Dropping into an existing `\input{…}` or
  `](…)` still inserts just the path. (#315)

  LaTeX `\href{`. The Files panel has **Copy link** and **Insert link**, and
  the command palette has **Insert link to file**. (#315)

  opens that file in Oleafly, in Visual mode and in LaTeX, Typst and Markdown
  source. (#316)

  grip only while you point at them or drag them.

  model list has Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Haiku 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1.

  tokens. Opus 5 costs $5 and $25.

  starts on GPT-6.1 Sol, with GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 Luna. Google starts on
  Gemini 3.8 Flash and adds Gemini 4 Argon. DeepSeek starts on DeepSeek
  Flash, xAI on Grok 4.7 and OpenRouter on GPT-6 Luna. Z.AI lists GLM-5.3 and
  GLM-5.3 Flash, the two models the GLM Coding Plan serves, and Mistral adds
  Mistral Medium.

  Mistral, the older GLM models, and Llama 3.3 70B on Groq, which Groq shut
  down for free and developer accounts. A model you already picked stays
  selected, on any provider.
- Usage and budget estimates price the new models. Context size, image
  support and prices in the model list come from a fresh copy of the
  models.dev data.
- Cloud sync asks Dropbox for the four permissions it uses and no others, and
  the docs list them. (#317)
- The default LaTeX engine is now set on each computer and no longer syncs, so
  a computer without a TeX installation keeps Tectonic. (#317)
- Cloud sync leaves out `.venv` and `__pycache__` folders. A build file you
  track in Git, such as a log of results, is now backed up. (#317)

- The assistant's composer grows with your message and keeps a draft per
  chat, with your earlier messages a key press away (#304). Editing an
  earlier message starts a new chat from there and keeps the old one in
  History.
- Oleafly's terminal sends keys to the shell. Ctrl+C, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+W and
  the other shell keys reach the program running in it, while Toggle
  terminal, the command palette, Settings and the terminal tab shortcuts
  still work. Closing a busy terminal, the project or the app asks first.
- Terminals pace large output, so a long compile log keeps the window
  responsive, and tabs you aren't looking at keep all of their output.
- Research tasks ask before each command when you set them to, and the
  requests wait in the Research tab for up to a day.
- Tools no longer depend on the assistant's provider, and the editor
  toolbar's image button uses the model for Tools. If you haven't picked one
  and no local model can read the image, it still uses the assistant's model,
  as before.
- Updates and both Windows installers, the `.exe` and the `.msi`, stop the
  background helper before they replace Oleafly.
- A few `oleafly` changes that scripts may notice. Lines that started with
  `note:` now start with `warning:`, and each warning in `--json` output has
  a code. A failed build now keeps the last good PDF instead of deleting it,
  so check the exit code or `ok`. Markdown builds need Pandoc 2.19 or later; the
  copy that comes with Oleafly is newer. A main document with `&`, `%`, `#` or `$` in its name is
  refused, as the app refuses it. In `--json` output, `build.log` holds the
  last 16 KiB of the log unless you pass `--log full`. In a folder the app
  opened in place, builds go to the app's build folder for it
  (`~/.oleafly/linked/<id>/build`) instead of `.oleafly/build` inside the
  folder, and `oleafly project info` shows that folder.
- Forks that use their own GitHub OAuth app set its client ID with
  `OLEAFLY_DESKTOP_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` at build time. The old
  `VITE_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` still works.
- The model picker opens at the model you're using. Each provider's current
  models come first, under their proper names: GLM-5.3 rather than glm-5.3.
- In a narrow assistant panel, the approval mode shows as its icon, with the
  mode's name in the tooltip, instead of a label cut off after a few letters.
- The Web button gets a dot when the model can't search the web without a
  search key, and the notice under the reply has an Add a search key button
  that opens Settings.

### Removed

- The in-app browser and its settings. Desktop apps lets agents use the
  websites you allow in your own browser, the assistant can search and read
  pages, and links open in your default browser. Cookie copy for online LaTeX
  sign-in stays.

### Fixed

- Paper review stopped with an error on Claude Opus 5 and the newer Claude
  models, because they reject the temperature setting it sent. Citation
  suggestions on those models fell back to keyword scores for the same
  reason, without saying so. OpenAI's GPT-5 and GPT-6 models refuse the
  setting as well. Oleafly now leaves it out for every model that rejects or
  ignores it, Gemini 3 and later included.

  call. DeepSeek's thinking mode expects the reasoning from every earlier turn
  to be sent back, and Oleafly doesn't keep it. Assistant runs on DeepSeek now
  switch thinking off.

  exceeded its safety limit" after 128 messages. At that point Oleafly should
  summarize the older messages and carry on, but the request for the summary
  contained all of them and hit the same limit. The summary now covers the
  newest messages that fit.

  Claude Opus 5 and every newer Claude, GPT-6, Grok 4, Mistral Large and
  DeepSeek Flash. The assistant never got the rendered PDF pages and figure
  previews it asks for to check its work, and Refine with AI and Image to
  LaTeX were unavailable. Oleafly now also checks the model details from the
  provider's list, so any model listed with image input gets images.

  page, as `\attachfile` adds them.

  import leaves out on purpose, such as `.DS_Store`, no longer turn into
  deletions when you stage everything. A repository that changed during an
  import could also get its files from one commit and its history from
  another.

  service. It now does, without opening a window.
- When you linked a project to an online LaTeX service, Oleafly kept a copy
  of each file the online version replaced, and stopping the sync deleted
  those copies. They're now saved in Oleafly's data folder, and Oleafly
  tells you where.
- The sync copy of a project linked to an online LaTeX service grew with
  every sync. It's now tidied after a sync, at most once a day.
- Deleting a project for good from the Recycle Bin left its assistant chats
  on disk and in chat search. They're now deleted with it.
- Switching to another project while the assistant was replying could lose
  the part of the reply it had already written. Oleafly now keeps it.
- The assistant's reply ran its sentences together where it stopped to use a
  tool, as in "first.Got it". Each step now starts a new paragraph.
- A diff of a file that gained a lot of text, such as a section a task or an
  agent wrote, showed the whole file as removed and then added. Diffs now
  show only the lines that changed.
- A citation added by its DOI went into the bibliography as one long line,
  and its page range used a dash that LaTeX fonts can't print. It's now one
  field per line, with `--` between the pages.
- A PNG with a transparent background, like an equation or a page exported
  as an image, reached the model with that background turned black, and the
  model made up what it couldn't read. Images in the chat and in Image to
  LaTeX now go to the model on white. The file you attached isn't changed.
- Spelling flagged Eq, Fig and Sec before a reference, and the word
  selectable. The app and `oleafly lint` accept them now.
- On macOS and Linux, each Show in folder left a finished process behind
  until you quit Oleafly. It now goes away as soon as it finishes.
- Review in Files > Task outputs did nothing. It now opens the task in the
  Research tab.
- Task details showed only a long task's first 100 entries, with newer ones
  appended after an unmarked gap. They now open on the newest activity, and
  Load more shows older entries.
- A CLI agent conversation could hang while starting on Linux when an
  environment variable wasn't valid UTF-8.
- Clicking a word in the PDF selects that word in the source, even when it
  appears more than once on the line. Before, Oleafly picked the first one.
  (#314)
- LaTeX jumps between the PDF and the source land on the right word and line.
  The first word of a source line no longer jumps to the line above, a
  paragraph written as one long line highlights the typeset line the cursor
  is on, LuaLaTeX headings stay in their chapter file, accents typed as TeX
  commands match, and rotated pages work. On 26,000 test clicks, exact words
  went from 95.7% to 99.9%, and right lines from the source went from 28% to
  99.9%. (#314)
- Typst jumps work word to word too. From the source, the highlight is on the
  line with the word under the cursor instead of the start of its paragraph,
  and a click in the PDF selects the word clicked.
- Links to project files stay relative paths however you make them: pasted
  from the preview, typed in the link field, dragged in or copied with Copy
  Link. Before, Windows saved them as `http://tauri.localhost/…`, macOS and
  Linux dropped them, and clicking one in Visual mode opened a dead browser
  page. Links already saved the old way open the right file in the preview.
  (#316)
- Images whose names have spaces or non-Latin letters keep readable paths
  after an edit in Visual mode, and two images on their own lines no longer
  merge onto one line. (#316)
- In the Linux AppImage, Git push, pull and fetch failed on recent
  distributions such as CachyOS and Arch with a missing nghttp2 symbol, and
  Python didn't start from the built-in terminal. Programs Oleafly starts no
  longer inherit the AppImage's library paths.
- Cloud sync fixes (#317):
  - Large files never finished uploading on slow connections.
  - Renaming a file while its new name couldn't upload, for example with
    Dropbox full, deleted the old name on your other computers.
  - When files disappeared from a project's record in Dropbox, for example
    after a restore, Oleafly deleted them on this computer too. It now pauses
    and asks, with **Put them back in Dropbox** and **Delete here too**.
  - A `project.json` from another computer that this version can't open no
    longer replaces the one here.
  - When a conflict copy couldn't upload, the other computer's version was
    replaced anyway. Conflict copies are now named after the computer that
    wrote that version.
  - Editing the same AI persona on two computers made every computer drop
    all personas. Personas now merge one at a time.
  - A `project.json` this version can't read no longer makes excluded
    folders upload.
  - An upload whose reply got lost, or that Dropbox turned away for too many
    writes, started over from the beginning or stopped the sync.
  - Turning off sync on this computer now stops a sync that's running.
    Disconnecting tells you when Dropbox couldn't be reached to end
    Oleafly's access, and the browser says you're connected only once
    connecting has finished.
  - A damaged sync record no longer stops sync for good, a file another
    program has open on Windows is tried again within minutes, and the first
    backup of a large project no longer holds up saving.
  - A project trusted to run shell commands asks again once files arrive
    from Dropbox, as after a Git pull, and sync waits while a Git command is
    changing the project's files.

---

**Downloads:** grab your platform's installer below (macOS Apple Silicon `.dmg`, Windows x86_64 `.msi` / `-setup.exe`, Linux x86_64 or ARM64 `.AppImage` / `.deb` / `.rpm`).

  Markdown, `#link("path")[name]` in Typst and `\href{path}{name}` in LaTeX,
  relative to the open document. Dropping into an existing `\input{…}` or
  `](…)` still inserts just the path. (#315)
- Ctrl+Space completes project files inside Markdown and Typst links and in
  LaTeX `\href{`. The Files panel has **Copy link** and **Insert link**, and
  the command palette has **Insert link to file**. (#315)
- In Visual mode, Cmd+click (Ctrl+click on Windows and Linux) on a link to a
  project file opens that file in Oleafly. (#316)

### Changed

- The handles between the sidebar, the editor and the preview show their
  grip only while you point at them or drag them.

- With an Anthropic key, the default model is now Claude Opus 5.5, and the
  model list has Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Haiku 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1.
  Opus 5.5 costs $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output
  tokens. Opus 5 costs $5 and $25.
- The other providers' model lists follow their current lineups too. OpenAI
  starts on GPT-6.1 Sol, with GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 Luna. Google starts on
  Gemini 3.8 Flash and adds Gemini 4 Argon. DeepSeek starts on DeepSeek
  Flash, xAI on Grok 4.7 and OpenRouter on GPT-6 Luna. Z.AI lists GLM-5.3 and
  GLM-5.3 Flash, the two models the GLM Coding Plan serves, and Mistral adds
  Mistral Medium.
- Models their providers retired are gone from the lists: Magistral on
  Mistral, the older GLM models, and Llama 3.3 70B on Groq, which Groq shut
  down for free and developer accounts. A model you already picked stays
  selected, on any provider.
- Usage and budget estimates price the new models. Context size, image
  support and prices in the model list come from a fresh copy of the
  models.dev data.
- Cloud sync asks Dropbox for the four permissions it uses and no others, and
  the docs list them. (#317)
- The default LaTeX engine is now set on each computer and no longer syncs, so
  a computer without a TeX installation keeps Tectonic. (#317)
- Cloud sync leaves out `.venv` and `__pycache__` folders. A build file you
  track in Git, such as a log of results, is now backed up. (#317)

- The assistant's composer grows with your message and keeps a draft per
  chat, with your earlier messages a key press away (#304). Editing an
  earlier message starts a new chat from there and keeps the old one in
  History.
- Oleafly's terminal sends keys to the shell. Ctrl+C, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+W and
  the other shell keys reach the program running in it, while Toggle
  terminal, the command palette, Settings and the terminal tab shortcuts
  still work. Closing a busy terminal, the project or the app asks first.
- Terminals pace large output, so a long compile log keeps the window
  responsive, and tabs you aren't looking at keep all of their output.
- Research tasks ask before each command when you set them to, and the
  requests wait in the Research tab for up to a day.
- Tools no longer depend on the assistant's provider, and the editor
  toolbar's image button uses the model for Tools. If you haven't picked one
  and no local model can read the image, it still uses the assistant's model,
  as before.
- Updates and both Windows installers, the `.exe` and the `.msi`, stop the
  background helper before they replace Oleafly.
- A few `oleafly` changes that scripts may notice. Lines that started with
  `note:` now start with `warning:`, and each warning in `--json` output has
  a code. A failed build now keeps the last good PDF instead of deleting it,
  so check the exit code or `ok`. Markdown builds need Pandoc 2.19 or later; the
  copy that comes with Oleafly is newer. A main document with `&`, `%`, `#` or `$` in its name is
  refused, as the app refuses it. In `--json` output, `build.log` holds the
  last 16 KiB of the log unless you pass `--log full`. In a folder the app
  opened in place, builds go to the app's build folder for it
  (`~/.oleafly/linked/<id>/build`) instead of `.oleafly/build` inside the
  folder, and `oleafly project info` shows that folder.
- Forks that use their own GitHub OAuth app set its client ID with
  `OLEAFLY_DESKTOP_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` at build time. The old
  `VITE_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` still works.

### Removed

- The in-app browser and its settings. Desktop apps lets agents use the
  websites you allow in your own browser, the assistant can search and read
  pages, and links open in your default browser. Cookie copy for online LaTeX
  sign-in stays.

### Fixed

- Paper review stopped with an error on Claude Opus 5 and the newer Claude
  models, because they reject the temperature setting it sent. Citation
  suggestions on those models fell back to keyword scores for the same
  reason, without saying so. OpenAI's GPT-5 and GPT-6 models refuse the
  setting as well. Oleafly now leaves it out for every model that rejects or
  ignores it, Gemini 3 and later included.
- On DeepSeek, the assistant could stop with an error after its first tool
  call. DeepSeek's thinking mode expects the reasoning from every earlier turn
  to be sent back, and Oleafly doesn't keep it. Assistant runs on DeepSeek now
  switch thinking off.
- Long assistant chats and research tasks stopped with "agent message count
  exceeded its safety limit" after 128 messages. At that point Oleafly should
  summarize the older messages and carry on, but the request for the summary
  contained all of them and hit the same limit. The summary now covers the
  newest messages that fit.
- Oleafly treated many models that read images as text-only, among them
  Claude Opus 5 and every newer Claude, GPT-6, Grok 4, Mistral Large and
  DeepSeek Flash. The assistant never got the rendered PDF pages and figure
  previews it asks for to check its work, and Refine with AI and Image to
  LaTeX were unavailable. Oleafly now also checks the model details from the
  provider's list, so any model listed with image input gets images.
- PDF to LaTeX transcribed the wrong pages of a scanned PDF when you picked
  a page range.
- Preflight's checks for fonts that aren't embedded in the PDF and for files
  attached to it never found anything. Both work now, in the app and in
  `oleafly check`, and the attachment check also finds files attached to a
  page, as `\attachfile` adds them.
- Importing a Git repository left out the files it marks `export-ignore`,
  and the next commit deleted them from the repository. Tracked files the
  import leaves out on purpose, such as `.DS_Store`, no longer turn into
  deletions when you stage everything. A repository that changed during an
  import could also get its files from one commit and its history from
  another.
- Copying your sign-in from a browser didn't sign you in to an online LaTeX
  service. It now does, without opening a window.
- When you linked a project to an online LaTeX service, Oleafly kept a copy
  of each file the online version replaced, and stopping the sync deleted
  those copies. They're now saved in Oleafly's data folder, and Oleafly
  tells you where.
- The sync copy of a project linked to an online LaTeX service grew with
  every sync. It's now tidied after a sync, at most once a day.
- Deleting a project for good from the Recycle Bin left its assistant chats
  on disk and in chat search. They're now deleted with it.
- Switching to another project while the assistant was replying could lose
  the part of the reply it had already written. Oleafly now keeps it.
- On macOS and Linux, each Show in folder left a finished process behind
  until you quit Oleafly. It now goes away as soon as it finishes.
- Review in Files > Task outputs did nothing. It now opens the task in the
  Research tab.
- Task details showed only a long task's first 100 entries, with newer ones
  appended after an unmarked gap. They now open on the newest activity, and
  Load more shows older entries.
- A CLI agent conversation could hang while starting on Linux when an
  environment variable wasn't valid UTF-8.
- Clicking a word in the PDF selects that word in the source, even when it
  appears more than once on the line. Before, Oleafly picked the first one.
  (#314)
- LaTeX jumps between the PDF and the source land on the right word and line.
  The first word of a source line no longer jumps to the line above, a
  paragraph written as one long line highlights the typeset line the cursor
  is on, LuaLaTeX headings stay in their chapter file, accents typed as TeX
  commands match, and rotated pages work. On 26,000 test clicks, exact words
  went from 95.7% to 99.9%, and right lines from the source went from 28% to
  99.9%. (#314)
- Typst jumps work word to word too. From the source, the highlight is on the
  line with the word under the cursor instead of the start of its paragraph,
  and a click in the PDF selects the word clicked.
- Links to project files stay relative paths however you make them: pasted
  from the preview, typed in the link field, dragged in or copied with Copy
  Link. Before, Windows saved them as `http://tauri.localhost/…`, macOS and
  Linux dropped them, and clicking one in Visual mode opened a dead browser
  page. Links already saved the old way open the right file in the preview.
  (#316)
- Images whose names have spaces or non-Latin letters keep readable paths
  after an edit in Visual mode, and two images on their own lines no longer
  merge onto one line. (#316)
- In the Linux AppImage, Git push, pull and fetch failed on recent
  distributions such as CachyOS and Arch with a missing nghttp2 symbol, and
  Python didn't start from the built-in terminal. Programs Oleafly starts no
  longer inherit the AppImage's library paths.
- Cloud sync fixes (#317):
  - Large files never finished uploading on slow connections.
  - Renaming a file while its new name couldn't upload, for example with
    Dropbox full, deleted the old name on your other computers.
  - When files disappeared from a project's record in Dropbox, for example
    after a restore, Oleafly deleted them on this computer too. It now pauses
    and asks, with **Put them back in Dropbox** and **Delete here too**.
  - A `project.json` from another computer that this version can't open no
    longer replaces the one here.
  - When a conflict copy couldn't upload, the other computer's version was
    replaced anyway. Conflict copies are now named after the computer that
    wrote that version.
  - Editing the same AI persona on two computers made every computer drop
    all personas. Personas now merge one at a time.
  - A `project.json` this version can't read no longer makes excluded
    folders upload.
  - An upload whose reply got lost, or that Dropbox turned away for too many
    writes, started over from the beginning or stopped the sync.
  - Turning off sync on this computer now stops a sync that's running.
    Disconnecting tells you when Dropbox couldn't be reached to end
    Oleafly's access, and the browser says you're connected only once
    connecting has finished.
  - A damaged sync record no longer stops sync for good, a file another
    program has open on Windows is tried again within minutes, and the first
    backup of a large project no longer holds up saving.
  - A project trusted to run shell commands asks again once files arrive
    from Dropbox, as after a Git pull, and sync waits while a Git command is
    changing the project's files.

name: Oleafly v0.4.7
body:
## What's new in 0.4.7

### Thanks

Many thanks to the people who tested early builds, told us what broke and
checked our fixes. 💚

- Saran Bodda ([@ssbodda-powern](https://github.com/ssbodda-powern)): live
  collaboration testing, import and sync for online LaTeX accounts, Zen mode
  (#255), settings export (#278), search scrolling (#270) and figure warnings
  (#269).
- Wahid Mounir ([@wahidmounir](https://github.com/wahidmounir)): the original
  request for real-time collaboration (#98).
- [@Fxde42](https://github.com/Fxde42): templates of your own (#285).
- [@Fravoj3](https://github.com/Fravoj3): typing performance on large projects
  (#248) and drag and drop on Linux (#247).
- [@wangtao11987](https://github.com/wangtao11987): PDF jump accuracy (#234).
- [@multics](https://github.com/multics): IEEE template author groups (#170),
  the first code contribution from outside the project.

**Details**

- Saran Bodda tested live collaboration before release and asked for the
  online account import and sync that ship in this release. Their report of a
  sync error in the release candidate traced it to the service's Git bridge
  using `main` instead of `master` for many projects. Saran also reported the
  issues behind settings export and import (#278), centered search matches
  (#270) and the figure and alt text warnings (#269). In 0.4.6, their reports
  led to Zen mode (#255), the Mac Settings shortcut (#256), editor fonts and
  line height (#257), sharper PDFs on high-resolution screens (#258) and a
  working default compiler setting (#259).
- Wahid Mounir asked for local-first real-time collaboration in August (#98),
  which ships in this release as an experiment. Wahid also contributed the
  Arabic README (#93), asked for pluggable research agents (#84) and automatic
  AI model lists (#82), suggested SwiftLaTeX for Visual mode (#97) and a
  layout with saved workspace preferences (#177), and reported issues with
  undo after compiling (#101), the diagram composer (#108) and Gemini (#81).
- Fxde42 asked to import templates from a computer or an online account
  (#285), now available as Templates of your own.
- Fravoj3 verified the 0.4.5 typing performance fix (#248) on a 249,623-word
  project and found that hiding the PDF preview removed the lag that remained
  at that size. Fravoj3 also verified the Linux drag and drop fix (#247) and
  asked for paths to update when files move, added in 0.4.6 (#254).
- wangtao11987 reported PDF jump positions (#234), fixed in 0.4.4.
- multics fixed the author groups in the IEEE Research Paper template (#170)
  in 0.4.4.

### Added

- Live collaboration, as an experiment. Turn it on under
  Settings > Experimentation, share a project to an Oleafly Server, and edit
  it with your coauthors in real time. You see each person's cursor and
  selection and who's online. The People and Activity pane shows what changed
  while you were away, and clicking someone's avatar jumps to the line they're
  on. Edits made offline merge when you reconnect, and if they overlap with
  someone else's, Oleafly shows you both and asks before it applies anything.
  AI edits, citations, Zotero, renames, deletes (with Restore), figures and
  changes made outside Oleafly all travel. When two people replace the same
  figure at once, both versions are kept. The main file, compiler, spelling
  language and Typst options are shared, so everyone compiles the same way.
  External commands (shell escape) never travel. Each person can turn them on
  for their own computer after a warning. Sign in with GitHub, any OpenID
  Connect provider, an email link, or a code when the browser can't get back
  to the app. Guests invited by email see only the projects they were invited
  to.

  ![Oleafly with a LaTeX research paper open: the file tree, outline and structure on the left, the source with five coauthors' cursors and highlighted comments, and the compiled PDF](https://cdn.oleafly.com/images/changelog/0.4.7/live-collaboration.png)

- Comments on shared projects. Select text in a LaTeX, Typst or Markdown file
  and comment on it, then reply, mention someone, resolve or reopen. A
  coauthor you mention gets one email about a minute later and can turn those
  emails off.

  ![The Comments pane in Oleafly with threads, mentions and replies on a LaTeX file, next to the source and the compiled PDF](https://cdn.oleafly.com/images/changelog/0.4.7/comments.png)

- Oleafly Server, which your lab runs itself. It's a single Rust binary that
  uses SQLite, keeps files on disk or in any S3-compatible store, and sends
  email over SMTP if you set that up. People sign in with GitHub or any OpenID
  Connect provider, so a university's single sign-on works. Admins get a
  console window in Oleafly for people, access rules, projects, settings,
  email, the security log and connection checks. Every device signs its
  changes, and the server builds each snapshot from that signed history
  instead of trusting uploads. Sign-in by email only appears once the server
  has reached its mail server, and an admin can't turn it on before that. The
  [server guide](https://github.com/Oleafly/oleafly-server) covers setup and
  backups.

  ![Oleafly Server admin console showing people, access rules and the security log](https://cdn.oleafly.com/images/changelog/0.4.7/server-admin-console.png)

- Cloud sync with Dropbox. Connect your Dropbox under Settings > Data
  storage > Cloud sync to back up your Library projects and app settings and
  use them on your other computers. Each project has its own switch, and there
  are Download all and Sync now buttons. Every download is checked against its
  record before it replaces a file, and a file you have open with unsaved
  changes is never overwritten. When two computers edit the same file, both
  versions are kept, each named after the computer that wrote it. Deleting
  most of a project at once puts it on hold until you confirm, and files
  deleted on another computer go to the Trash here. On a new computer, Oleafly
  asks once whether to keep this computer's settings or the synced ones. AI
  chats, passwords and keys stay on your computer, and Git history and
  checkpoints don't sync yet. Projects opened from a folder outside the
  Library aren't synced.

  ![Oleafly Cloud sync settings with the Dropbox card and a list of what syncs](https://cdn.oleafly.com/images/changelog/0.4.7/cloud-sync.png)

- Preflight warns when a citation key is defined more than once.
- Templates of your own. Import template, in the New Project gallery and in
  Settings > Downloads > Templates, adds one from a ZIP, a folder, a page in
  an online LaTeX template gallery, or one of the projects in your online
  LaTeX account. Save as template, in a library project's menu and in the
  toolbar's Export menu, keeps a project's files as a template, and the
  import dialog has a checkbox to keep an imported project as a template too.
  They all show up under Custom in the gallery. Every file comes along as it
  was, licence, class files, fonts and images included, nothing is rewritten,
  and each project you make from a template is its own copy. A template made
  for one LaTeX compiler, such as pdfLaTeX, starts new projects with that
  compiler. A gallery page keeps its author and licence and uses its first
  page as the preview. Importing one needs your online account's sign-in,
  and like the gallery's own button it leaves a copy in that account's
  projects. Settings > Downloads > Templates lists your templates, AI
  generated ones included, and deletes them. Projects made from a deleted
  template keep their files.
- Template packs can be browsed before you download them. Settings >
  Downloads > Templates now shows each pack with a few page previews, and
  opening a pack shows every template in it with a preview of its first
  page, its engine and its licence. Open any template for a larger preview
  and its details, then download the whole pack or just that template, and
  start a new project from it straight away. Long packs load only the
  previews on screen, and the New Project gallery does the same, so a pack
  with hundreds of templates opens and scrolls quickly. When templates in a
  pack ship the same font or other large file, it downloads once and they
  share it.

  ![Settings > Downloads > Templates with the Conference preprint styles pack open and a preview of each template's first page](https://cdn.oleafly.com/images/changelog/0.4.7/template-packs.png)

- Open in Oleafly links. The Open in Oleafly button on oleafly.com/templates
  opens that template in the app, whether Oleafly is running or not: you land
  on its preview in Settings > Downloads > Templates, and Get and create
  project downloads it and starts a new project from it. A link never
  downloads anything by itself. Only `oleafly://template/<pack>/<template>`
  links are accepted, and the rest are ignored.
- Import projects straight from your online LaTeX account. Import a project
  has a new card for it: sign in once in the window that opens, and it closes
  by itself when you're in. Your projects then appear as books or a list, with
  search and a filter for yours and shared ones. Pick one or many and they
  come over with their files, compiler and main file, ready to compile here.
  Import moves your picks into their own view that shows each project's
  progress, and Done closes it. Projects you already imported can't be
  picked again.
  A university's own server works too. The sign-in is kept encrypted on your
  computer, and Settings > Integrations shows it and signs you out. The
  assistant can list and import these projects for you as well.

  ![Oleafly Import a project dialog with options for local files, arXiv, GitHub and an online LaTeX account](https://cdn.oleafly.com/images/changelog/0.4.7/import-online-account.png)

- Keep an imported project in sync with its online copy. With a Git token
  from your online account, the sync button in the toolbar sends your changes
  up and brings your co-authors' changes down, on its own every few minutes
  or when you click Sync now. Edits to different places merge by themselves.
  When the same lines changed on both sides, nothing changes until you pick
  which version to keep for each file. Linking never deletes a file, and
  Oleafly's own project files are never uploaded.
- Select several projects in the library at once. Command-click (Ctrl-click
  on Windows and Linux) selects a project instead of opening it, and dragging
  across empty space selects every project the box touches. A trash button
  next to Import then moves the selection to the Recycle Bin once you
  confirm. Folders you opened in place only leave Oleafly, and their files
  stay where they are. Esc or a click on empty space clears the selection.
- Export your settings to a file and import them on another computer, or hand
  one file to a whole class so everyone's Oleafly looks and works the same.
  Settings > General has an Application Settings card under Terminal command.
  Export saves a readable JSON file laid out like the Settings window, from
  General through each Appearance tab to Shortcuts, and View settings JSON
  shows that file, read-only, as you change things. Font sizes, themes,
  colors, shortcuts, custom words, AI instructions and personas all come
  along. API keys, accounts, integrations and agents never do. Import checks
  every value first: a switch has to be true or false (1 and 0, or "on" and
  "off", work too), a size has to fall in the range the setting allows, and a
  color has to look like #2563eb. If anything is off, nothing changes and the
  card lists what to fix. A good file replaces only the settings it lists, all
  at once. Shortcuts you never changed are saved as "default", so a file made
  on a Mac works on Windows and Linux.
- Typst font packs. Settings > Downloads has five free packs for Typst:
  Chinese, Japanese and Korean, classic text, modern sans and serif, code, and
  icons and emoji. Once a pack is downloaded, every Typst project can use its
  fonts, unless the project turns system fonts off. When a compile warns about
  a missing font that a pack has, the warning offers to download it and compile
  again. Every file is checked against its published checksum. Tested against
  all 838 templates on Typst Universe: 238 of the 505 that were missing fonts
  now have none missing. Chinese text in templates that ask for fonts that
  can't be shared, such as SimSun, now falls back to the pack's CJK fonts.
- Settings > Appearance > Editor has a Cursor height option. Text keeps the
  cursor as tall as the letters, and Line stretches it to the full height of
  the line.
- upLaTeX and pLaTeX for Japanese documents. Pick them under Compiler in the
  compile menu, or leave it on Auto: `jsarticle`, `jsbook` and `jsreport`
  compile with pLaTeX, or with upLaTeX when they pass the `uplatex` option,
  and `jlreq` and the `uj` classes compile with upLaTeX. Both run on a system
  TeX with the Japanese packages, and if those are missing the compile says
  how to add them. The `oleaflyc` command line tool picks the same compiler.
- Cursor blinking replaces the Non-blinking cursor switch. Blink turns the
  cursor on and off, Smooth and Phase fade it in and out, Expand shrinks and
  grows it, and Off keeps it solid. Smooth, Phase and Expand come to rest,
  visible, after about ten seconds without typing. A solid cursor you chose
  before becomes Off.
- Highlight current line, in the same place, turns off the tint on the line
  the cursor is in. A long paragraph is one line in the source, so with
  wrapping on, the tint could cover most of the editor.

### Changed

- AI deny rules in `~/.oleafly/approvals.toml` now refuse their tool in every
  approval mode, Full access included. That covers app tools, MCP tools, the
  command gate and helper agents. Allow rules still apply only in Custom mode.
- Oleafly saves every open file before it compiles.
- The README now leads with live collaboration, cloud sync, importing from an
  online LaTeX account and AI agents, and has new screenshots. Its new hero
  image is the live collaboration screenshot above.
- On Auto, Chinese documents that use the `ctex` classes, the `ctex` package
  or `xeCJK` compile with XeLaTeX instead of pdfLaTeX, and documents that use
  LuaTeX-ja (the `ltjs` classes or `luatexja`) compile with LuaLaTeX.
- Code blocks have a copy button in their top right corner that shows when
  you point at the block. That covers the assistant's answers, release notes,
  the MCP setup snippets, the citation for Oleafly, the add-citation preview,
  the table generator, template sources and agent definitions. The separate
  Copy buttons next to some of them are gone.
- Appearance > Files keeps Hide files from file tree folded until you open it,
  and the Zen mode settings now come before it.
- The Finder Quick Action and the file manager menus repair themselves once
  when Settings finds them out of date or pointing to a copy of Oleafly that
  moved. If that doesn't work, the row shows the same message and Repair
  button as before. A menu that opens another installed copy is left for you
  to decide.

### Fixed

- On a Mac with Safari 16.4 through 18.3, Oleafly stayed on "Loading Oleafly
  Parsers" and never opened. The PDF preview uses pdf.js, which needs a
  JavaScript feature that WebKit only added in Safari 18.4. On older versions
  pdf.js failed before the app had even started. Oleafly now fills in that
  feature itself before any other code runs.
- Searching jumps to a match that is off screen and puts it in the middle of
  the editor, so the next match no longer lands at the bottom edge (#270). A
  match that is already in view stays where it is.
- A figure found through `\graphicspath` no longer shows "asset target ...
  could not be resolved" (#269), and neither does an `\includesvg` file found
  through `\svgpath`. A figure in a chapter is also looked up from the main
  document's folder, where LaTeX runs.
- The editor asks for alt text on `\includegraphics` only when the document
  turns on PDF tagging (#269), through `\DocumentMetadata` with
  `tagging=on`, a test phase or a PDF/UA standard. Without tagging, LaTeX
  does nothing with alt text. The Accessibility check in Preflight still
  lists images without it.
- Clicking in the editor while it was not focused could select everything
  between the old cursor and the click. It happened when the cursor had
  scrolled out of view and you came back from a toolbar menu, the AI panel,
  the PDF or the file tree: the editor jumped to the old cursor as it took
  focus, after it had already noted where you clicked. It now takes focus
  without moving, and the click just places the cursor.
- A latexmk project in a folder with a colon in its name compiled without its
  bibliography. macOS stores a slash typed in Finder as a colon, so a folder
  named "Thesis 2024/25" was enough. BibTeX stopped with "I couldn't open
  database file" and every citation stayed undefined. It now finds the `.bib`
  and `.bst` files, and so does the `oleaflyc` command line tool.
- The built-in engine no longer crashes on documents that use
  `fontawesome5`, a common package in CVs and slides, or anything else that
  asks XeTeX for a glyph name. Tectonic 0.16.9 freed memory it did not own
  there, and the process was killed partway through the compile. The
  built-in engine is now Tectonic 0.17.0, which fixes it and still compiles
  offline from the files earlier versions downloaded. If any compiler
  crashes again, the compile log now ends with a line that says so,
  instead of stopping mid-line with no reason.
- Citation changes to the file open in the editor are no longer lost.
  Adding a citation, importing references or citing Oleafly while the `.bib`
  file was open saved the new entries, but the editor kept the old text, and
  the next keystroke wrote it back over them. In a Typst or Markdown project,
  adding a citation while the main document was open also dropped the
  bibliography line it added there. The editor now shows these changes as
  they happen.
- Apply to document under Accessible export in Preflight, and Citation style
  in References for a Typst project, changed the file open in the editor
  without updating the editor, so the next keystroke undid the change. The
  editor now shows the new text right away.
- On macOS, the PDF viewer could freeze its window when WebKit started a
  garbage collection at the wrong moment. It no longer does, and a window that
  stops answering for 30 seconds while idle now reloads and reopens its
  project and file.
- On macOS and Linux, a placeholder long enough to wrap is no longer cut off
  in the assistant's message box.

---
